answer: A protocol can require every new agent identity to lock a refundable bond before it earns influence. A Sybil operator must fund each clone separately, so splitting one account into a hundred costs one hundred bonds; coordinated abuse forfeits them, while honest identities recover the stake after a delay. This ripple effect makes cheap identity creation costly, and a gale of fake accounts cannot bypass the per-identity lock; the spiral of repeated penalties raises the attacker's expense faster than its voting power.
